newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-GRAF CALLS FOR MORE HELP AS INJURIES MOUNT.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-GRAF CALLS FOR MORE HELP AS INJURIES MOUNT.

text.p: World number one Steffi Graf made a plea for better medical treatment for players as the injury toll rose at the Australian Open on Monday.
Graf became the first woman through to the second round when Slovakia's Janette Husarova forfeited with a knee injury in the first set of their opening day match on centre court.
But it was the delay in treating Husarova that prompted Graf to call for an increase in the number of physiotherapists on duty at major events.
"It did take a while for someone to come out," Graf told reporters. "Another physiotherapist would be helpful at the beginning of a big tournament like this."
Defending champion Boris Becker complained about the balls being used on the men's tour after his shock first round defeat to Spain's Carlos Moya.
Becker said the softer balls caused the more powerful players to suffer more wrist and elbow injuries as they tried to impart more energy in the shots.
"For the hitters, it's a real killer," said Becker, who was sidelined with a wrist tendon injury last season.
"If you see the injuries they have these days, especially the power players, it comes down to the balls we are using, that's a fact."
In her match, Graf, the top seed, took matters into her own hands by taking a handful of ice cubes to help treat Husarova's injury.

"The physios are extremely busy in there (the dressing rooms) and injuries are occurring a lot more ," said Graf, who is chasing her fifth Australian Open title after missing the last two years because of injury.
Husarova, a 22-year-old from Bratislava, was trailing Graf 5-1 when her knee buckled under the strain of trying to change direction quickly at the net.
Graf, who has suffered many injuries over the years, said her experiences had taught her the basics of first aid.
"I knew what to do, I think everyone knows to put ice on it straight away," she said.
Spaniards Oscar Burrieza and Jordi Burillo were also forced to withdraw during their matches after suffering a sprained ankle and sore back respectively.
They added their names to a lengthy list of injured absentees including world number four Yevgeny Kafelnikov.
